author: 최민재
title: Deep Graph Convolutional Networks for Incident-Driven Traffic Speed Prediction
authors: Qinge Xie, Tiancheng Guo, Yang Chen, Yu Xiao, Xin Wang, Ben Y. Zhao
abstract: Accurate traffic speed prediction is an important and challenging topic for transportation planning. Previous studies on traffic speed prediction predominately used spatio-temporal and context features for prediction. However, they have not made good use of the impact of traffic incidents. In this work, we aim to make use of the information of incidents to achieve a better prediction of traffic speed. Our incident-driven prediction framework consists of three processes. First, we propose a critical incident discovery method to discover traffic incidents with high impact on traffic speed. Second, we design a binary classifier, which uses deep learning methods to extract the latent incident impact features. Combining above methods, we propose a Deep Incident-Aware Graph Convolutional Network (DIGC-Net) to effectively incorporate traffic incident, spatio-temporal, periodic and context features for traffic speed prediction. We conduct experiments using two real-world traffic datasets of San Francisco and New York City. The results demonstrate the superior performance of our model compared with the competing benchmarks.
content: Traffic speed prediction에서 기존 연구는 spatio-temporal feature와 context feature를 주로 썼고 traffic incident의 영향은 잘 활용하지 못했다는 점에서 출발함. Incident 정보를 활용하는 incident-driven prediction framework를 제안하며 세 단계로 구성됨. 먼저 traffic speed에 큰 영향을 주는 incident를 찾는 critical incident discovery method를 제안하고, 다음으로 deep learning으로 latent incident impact feature를 추출하는 binary classifier를 설계함. 이를 결합해 incident, spatio-temporal, periodic, context feature를 모두 반영하는 Deep Incident-Aware Graph Convolutional Network(DIGC-Net)를 제안함. San Francisco와 New York City의 두 real-world dataset 실험에서 competing benchmark 대비 더 나은 성능을 보였다고 함.
memo: Incident를 external feature로 graph conv에 넣는 구조인데, 교통 쪽에서는 이런 event-driven forecasting이 당연한 방향 같음. 보행자 쪽에 대응시키면 신호 변화나 차량 접근 같은 event를 trajectory 모델의 conditioning으로 쓰는 것과 비슷한 발상. Baseline이 어떤 모델인지는 다음에 표를 자세히 볼 것.

author: 최민재
title: Social GAN: Socially Acceptable Trajectories with Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Agrim Gupta; Justin Johnson; Li Fei-Fei; Silvio Savarese; Alexandre Alahi
abstract: Understanding human motion behavior is critical for autonomous moving platforms (like self-driving cars and social robots) if they are to navigate human-centric environments. This is challenging because human motion is inherently multimodal: given a history of human motion paths, there are many socially plausible ways that people could move in the future. We tackle this problem by combining tools from sequence prediction and generative adversarial networks: a recurrent sequence-to-sequence model observes motion histories and predicts future behavior, using a novel pooling mechanism to aggregate information across people. We predict socially plausible futures by training adversarially against a recurrent discriminator, and encourage diverse predictions with a novel variety loss. Through experiments on several datasets we demonstrate that our approach outperforms prior work in terms of accuracy, variety, collision avoidance, and computational complexity.
content: 사람의 이동은 본질적으로 multimodal이라 같은 observed history에서도 socially plausible한 future가 여러 개 존재함. 이를 다루기 위해 sequence-to-sequence 기반 generator에 GAN을 결합한 Social GAN을 제안함. 핵심은 두 가지로, (1) 보행자 간 정보를 aggregate하는 새로운 pooling module과 (2) 다양한 sample을 유도하는 variety loss임. Generator는 recurrent encoder-decoder로 motion history를 보고 future를 예측하고, recurrent discriminator와 adversarial하게 학습시켜 socially acceptable한 trajectory를 만들게 함. 여러 dataset 실험에서 기존 Social-LSTM 대비 accuracy, variety, collision avoidance, computational complexity 측면에서 더 낫다고 보고함.
memo: Social-LSTM의 deterministic 한계를 generative로 푼 baseline 논문. Variety loss(best-of-K)는 지금 봐도 간단하고 쓸 만한데, K를 키우면 ADE/FDE가 좋아지기만 해서 metric이 diversity를 제대로 반영하는지는 의문. 내 연구에서 crosswalk 대기/진입 같은 discrete mode를 explicit하게 넣어보면 어떨까 생각함.

author: 최민재
title: Social-STGCNN: A Social Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Neural Network for Human Trajectory Prediction
authors: Abduallah Mohamed; Kun Qian; Mohamed Elhoseiny; Christian Claudel
abstract: Better machine understanding of pedestrian behaviors enables faster progress in modeling interactions between agents such as autonomous vehicles and humans. Pedestrian trajectories are not only influenced by the pedestrian itself but also by interaction with surrounding objects. Previous methods modeled these interactions by using a variety of aggregation methods that integrate different learned pedestrians states. We propose the Social Spatio-Temporal Graph Convolutional Neural Network (Social-STGCNN), which substitutes the need of aggregation methods by modeling the interactions as a graph. Our results show an improvement over the state of art by 20% on the Final Displacement Error (FDE) and an improvement on the Average Displacement Error (ADE) with 8.5 times less parameters and up to 48 times faster inference speed than previously reported methods. In addition, our model is data efficient, and exceeds previous state of the art on the ADE metric with only 20% of the training data. We propose a kernel function to embed the social interactions between pedestrians within the adjacency matrix. Through qualitative analysis, we show that our model inherited social behaviors that can be expected between pedestrians trajectories. Code is available at https://github.com/abduallahmohamed/Social-STGCNN.
content: Pedestrian trajectory는 자기 자신뿐 아니라 주변 agent와의 interaction에 영향을 받는데, 기존 방법은 interaction을 social pooling 같은 aggregation으로 처리했음. Social-STGCNN은 이를 aggregation 대신 graph로 모델링함. 각 시점의 보행자를 node로, 보행자 간 거리 기반 kernel function으로 weighted adjacency matrix를 구성해 social interaction을 embed하고, spatio-temporal graph convolution과 TXP-CNN으로 future 분포 parameter를 예측하는 구조임. 기존 SOTA 대비 FDE 20% 개선, ADE도 개선되었고 parameter는 8.5배 적고 inference는 최대 48배 빠르다고 함. 학습 데이터 20%만 써도 ADE에서 기존 SOTA를 넘는 data efficiency도 보임.
memo: LSTM 없이 CNN으로 temporal 부분을 처리해서 가볍다는 게 인상적임. 다만 adjacency가 거리 kernel 하나로 고정이라 heading이나 speed 차이 같은 정보가 안 들어감. 횡단보도에서는 vehicle-pedestrian 간 relative velocity가 더 중요할 텐데 kernel에 이걸 넣는 확장을 해볼 만함.

author: 최민재
title: Trajectron++: Dynamically-Feasible Trajectory Forecasting With Heterogeneous Data
authors: Tim Salzmann; Boris Ivanovic; Punarjay Chakravarty; Marco Pavone
abstract: Reasoning about human motion is an important prerequisite to safe and socially-aware robotic navigation. As a result, multi-agent behavior prediction has become a core component of modern human-robot interactive systems, such as self-driving cars. While there exist many methods for trajectory forecasting, most do not enforce dynamic constraints and do not account for environmental information (e.g., maps). Towards this end, we present Trajectron++, a modular, graph-structured recurrent model that forecasts the trajectories of a general number of diverse agents while incorporating agent dynamics and heterogeneous data (e.g., semantic maps). Trajectron++ is designed to be tightly integrated with robotic planning and control frameworks; for example, it can produce predictions that are optionally conditioned on ego-agent motion plans. We demonstrate its performance on several challenging real-world trajectory forecasting datasets, outperforming a wide array of state-of-the-art deterministic and generative methods.
content: Trajectron++는 graph-structured recurrent model로, 다양한 종류의 agent의 trajectory를 동시에 forecasting하는 modular framework임. 기존 방법 대부분이 dynamic constraint를 반영하지 않고 map 같은 environmental information도 쓰지 않는다는 점을 지적하고, agent dynamics와 heterogeneous data(semantic map 등)를 함께 통합함. Robotic planning/control과의 연동을 염두에 두고 설계되어, ego-agent의 motion plan에 conditioned된 prediction도 optional하게 가능함. 여러 real-world trajectory forecasting dataset에서 deterministic, generative 계열 SOTA 방법들을 앞섰다고 보고함. 보행자 예측 연구에서 거의 필수 baseline이라 정독함.
memo: Social-STGCNN이나 Social GAN은 ped-only인데 Trajectron++는 여러 종류 agent를 같은 틀에서 다루고 dynamics까지 넣은 게 큰 차이. 특히 ego-conditioned prediction이 pedestrian-vehicle interaction 쪽에 바로 쓰일 수 있어 보임. 내 crosswalk 데이터에 semantic map(crosswalk, sidewalk polygon)을 붙여서 돌려볼 계획.

author: 최민재
title: It Is Not the Journey but the Destination: Endpoint Conditioned Trajectory Prediction
authors: Karttikeya Mangalam; Harshayu Girase; Shreyas Agarwal; Kuan-Hui Lee; Ehsan Adeli; Jitendra Malik; et al.
abstract: Human trajectory forecasting with multiple socially interacting agents is of critical importance for autonomous navigation in human environments, e.g., for self-driving cars and social robots. In this work, we present Predicted Endpoint Conditioned Network (PECNet) for flexible human trajectory prediction. PECNet infers distant trajectory endpoints to assist in long-range multi-modal trajectory prediction. A novel non-local social pooling layer enables PECNet to infer diverse yet socially compliant trajectories. Additionally, we present a simple "truncation-trick" for improving few-shot multi-modal trajectory prediction performance. We show that PECNet improves state-of-the-art performance on the Stanford Drone trajectory prediction benchmark by ~20.9% and on the ETH/UCY benchmark by ~40.8%. Project homepage: https://karttikeya.github.io/publication/htf/
content: 장기 trajectory 예측에서 destination이 중요하다는 관점에서, 먼저 먼 endpoint를 추론하고 그에 conditioned해서 전체 경로를 예측하는 PECNet(Predicted Endpoint Conditioned Network)을 제안함. 보행자 간 non-local social pooling layer를 두어 다양하면서도 socially compliant한 trajectory를 추론하게 함. 또 few-shot multi-modal prediction 성능을 높이는 간단한 truncation-trick도 제안함. Stanford Drone benchmark에서 약 20.9%, ETH/UCY에서 약 40.8% 성능을 개선했다고 보고함.
memo: Goal-conditioned 구조라는 점에서 보행자가 어디로 가려는지(예: 횡단보도 반대편)가 먼저 정해지는 우리 setting에 잘 맞음. 단 endpoint를 CVAE로 sampling하는 부분이 학습 때 GT endpoint에 의존하는 만큼 endpoint 오류가 trajectory 전체로 전파되는 점은 확인이 필요함.

author: 최민재
title: Spatiotemporal Forecasting of Incidents and Congestion with Implications for Sustainable Traffic Control
authors: Tony Kinchen, Ting Bai, Nishanth Venkatesh S., Andreas A. Malikopoulos
abstract: Urban traffic anomalies, such as collisions and disruptions, threaten the safety, efficiency, and sustainability of transportation systems. In this paper, we present a simulation-based framework for modeling, detecting, and predicting such anomalies in urban networks. Using the Simulation of Urban MObility (SUMO) platform, we generate reproducible rear-end and intersection crash scenarios with matched baselines, enabling controlled experimentation and comparative evaluation. We record vehicle-level travel time, speed, and emissions for both edge- and network-level analysis. Building on this dataset, we develop a hybrid forecasting architecture that combines bidirectional long short-term memory networks with a diffusion convolutional recurrent neural network to capture temporal dynamics and spatial dependencies. Our simulation studies on the Broadway corridor in New York City demonstrate the framework's ability to reproduce consistent incident conditions, quantify their effects, and provide accurate multi-horizon traffic forecasts. Our results highlight the value of combining controlled anomaly generation with deep predictive models to support reproducible evaluation and sustainable traffic management.
content: Collision이나 disruption 같은 urban traffic anomaly가 교통 시스템의 safety, efficiency, sustainability를 위협한다는 문제의식에서, anomaly를 modeling, detecting, predicting하는 simulation-based framework를 제안함. SUMO(Simulation of Urban MObility)로 matched baseline이 있는 rear-end 및 intersection crash 시나리오를 재현 가능하게 생성하고, vehicle-level travel time, speed, emissions를 edge 및 network 수준에서 기록함. 이 dataset을 바탕으로 bidirectional LSTM과 diffusion convolutional recurrent neural network(DCRNN)를 결합한 hybrid forecasting architecture로 temporal dynamics와 spatial dependency를 함께 잡음. New York City의 Broadway corridor 시뮬레이션에서 일관된 incident 조건을 재현하고 영향을 정량화하며 multi-horizon forecast가 정확하다고 보고함.
memo: BiLSTM + DCRNN 조합이라 모델 자체의 novelty는 크지 않고 contribution은 simulation으로 controlled anomaly를 만든 쪽에 있다고 봄. SUMO로 만든 crash라서 real-world에서의 transfer는 의문. 그래도 SUMO 쪽 pedestrian 모델과 연결해서 보행자 사고 시나리오를 만드는 아이디어는 참고할 만함.

author: 최민재
title: Driving Behavior Based Relative Risk Evaluation Using a Nonparametric Optimization Method
venue: Int. J. Environ. Res. Public Health
authors: Qiong Bao,Hanrun Tang and Yongjun Shen
abstract: Evaluating risks when driving is a valuable method by which to make people better understand their driving behavior, and also provides the basis for improving driving performance. In many existing risk evaluation studies, however, most of the time only the occurrence frequency of risky driving events is considered in the time dimension and fixed weights allocation is adopted when constructing a risk evaluation model. In this study, we develop a driving behavior-based relative risk evaluation model using a nonparametric optimization method, in which both the frequency and the severity level of different risky driving behaviors are taken into account, and the concept of relative risk instead of absolute risk is proposed. In the case study, based on the data from a naturalistic driving experiment, various risky driving behaviors are identified, and the proposed model is applied to assess the overall risk related to the distance travelled by an individual driver during a specific driving segment, relative to other drivers on other segments, and it is further compared with an absolute risk evaluation. The results show that the proposed model is superior in avoiding the absolute risk quantification of all kinds of risky driving behaviors, and meanwhile, a prior knowledge on the contribution of different risky driving behaviors to the overall risk is not required. Such a model has a wide range of application scenarios, and is valuable for feedback research relating to safe driving, for a personalized insurance assessment based on drivers' behavior, and for the safety evaluation of professional drivers such as ride-hailing drivers.
content: 운전 중 risk evaluation은 운전자가 자기 driving behavior를 이해하고 성능을 개선하는 근거가 되는데, 기존 연구는 대개 risky driving event의 occurrence frequency만 보고 fixed weight allocation을 썼다는 한계를 지적함. 이 연구는 nonparametric optimization method로 risky driving behavior의 frequency와 severity level을 모두 고려하는 relative risk evaluation model을 제안하고, absolute risk 대신 relative risk 개념을 도입함. Naturalistic driving experiment 데이터에서 여러 risky behavior를 식별하고, 운전자 개인이 특정 구간에서 이동한 거리당 overall risk를 다른 운전자, 다른 구간 대비로 평가해 absolute risk와도 비교함. 결과적으로 모델이 absolute risk 정량화의 문제를 피하고 behavior별 risk 기여도에 대한 prior knowledge가 필요 없다고 함. Safe driving feedback, 개인화 보험 평가, 라이드헤일링 기사 같은 professional driver의 safety evaluation에도 활용 가능하다고 함.
memo: Weight를 사전에 정하지 않고 데이터에서 optimization으로 구한다는 점은 좋지만 relative risk가 실제 crash risk와 얼마나 맞는지 validation이 약한 것 같음. 내 분야와는 거리가 있지만, 보행자 risky crossing behavior를 relative risk로 scoring하는 데 같은 틀을 쓸 수 있을지 생각해봄.

author: 최민재
title: Social NCE: Contrastive Learning of Socially-aware Motion Representations
authors: Yuejiang Liu; Qi Yan; Alexandre Alahi
abstract: Learning socially-aware motion representations is at the core of recent advances in multi-agent problems, such as human motion forecasting and robot navigation in crowds. Despite promising progress, existing representations learned with neural networks still struggle to generalize in closed-loop predictions (e.g., output colliding trajectories). This issue largely arises from the non-i.i.d. nature of sequential prediction in conjunction with ill-distributed training data. Intuitively, if the training data only comes from human behaviors in safe spaces, i.e., from "positive" examples, it is difficult for learning algorithms to capture the notion of "negative" examples like collisions. In this work, we aim to address this issue by explicitly modeling negative examples through self-supervision: (i) we introduce a social contrastive loss that regularizes the extracted motion representation by discerning the ground-truth positive events from synthetic negative ones; (ii) we construct informative negative samples based on our prior knowledge of rare but dangerous circumstances. Our method substantially reduces the collision rates of recent trajectory forecasting, behavioral cloning and reinforcement learning algorithms, outperforming state-of-the-art methods on several benchmarks. Our code is available at https://github.com/vita-epfl/social-nce.
content: Social NCE는 socially-aware motion representation을 학습하기 위해 contrastive learning을 도입한 연구임. 기존 representation은 closed-loop prediction에서 collision이 나는 trajectory를 내놓는 경우가 많은데, 이는 training data가 safe space에서 얻은 positive example뿐이어서 collision 같은 negative example의 개념을 배우기 어렵기 때문이라고 진단함. 이를 위해 (1) ground-truth positive event와 synthetic negative를 구분하게 하는 social contrastive loss, (2) rare하지만 위험한 상황에 대한 prior knowledge로 informative negative sample을 만드는 방법을 제안함. Trajectory forecasting, behavioral cloning, RL 모두에서 collision rate를 크게 낮추고 여러 benchmark에서 SOTA 방법을 앞섰다고 함.
memo: Negative sample을 prior knowledge로 만든다는 발상이 좋음. 보행자-차량 near-miss를 negative로 정의해서 contrastive loss에 넣으면 crosswalk에서 safety-aware한 representation을 만들 수 있을 듯. Negative sampling 규칙을 hand-crafted로 정해야 해서 scene마다 일반화가 되는지가 의문.

author: 최민재
title: Coupling Intent and Action for Pedestrian Crossing Behavior Prediction
authors: Yu Yao; Ella Atkins; Matthew Johnson Roberson; Ram Vasudevan; Xiaoxiao Du
abstract: Accurate prediction of pedestrian crossing behaviors by autonomous vehicles can significantly improve traffic safety. Existing approaches often model pedestrian behaviors using trajectories or poses but do not offer a deeper semantic interpretation of a person's actions or how actions influence a pedestrian's intention to cross in the future. In this work, we follow the neuroscience and psychological literature to define pedestrian crossing behavior as a combination of an unobserved inner will (a probabilistic representation of binary intent of crossing vs. not crossing) and a set of multi-class actions (e.g., walking, standing, etc.). Intent generates actions, and the future actions in turn reflect the intent. We present a novel multi-task network that predicts future pedestrian actions and uses predicted future action as a prior to detect the present intent and action of the pedestrian. We also designed an attention relation network to incorporate external environmental contexts thus further improve intent and action detection performance. We evaluated our approach on two naturalistic driving datasets, PIE and JAAD, and extensive experiments show significantly improved and more explainable results for both intent detection and action prediction over state-of-the-art approaches. Our code is available at: https://github.com/umautobots/pedestrian_intent_action_detection.
content: 보행자 crossing behavior를 trajectory나 pose로만 모델링하는 기존 방식은 행동의 semantic한 의미나 action이 future crossing intention에 어떻게 영향을 주는지 설명하지 못함. 이 논문은 neuroscience와 psychology 문헌을 참고해 crossing behavior를 관측되지 않는 inner will(crossing vs not crossing의 binary intent를 확률적으로 표현)과 multi-class action(walking, standing 등)의 조합으로 정의함. Intent가 action을 만들고, future action이 다시 intent를 반영한다는 관점에서, 미래 action을 예측하고 이를 prior로 사용해 현재의 intent와 action을 detect하는 multi-task network를 제안함. 외부 환경 context를 반영하는 attention relation network도 추가함. PIE와 JAAD에서 intent detection과 action prediction 모두 SOTA 대비 개선되고 더 explainable한 결과를 보였다고 함.
memo: Intent를 latent, action을 observable로 분리해서 둘을 coupling한 설계가 깔끔함. Trajectory-only 모델과 달리 standing이 곧 not-crossing이 아니라는 구분이 가능해서 crosswalk 대기 행동 분석에 유용해 보임. Action label이 필요해서 annotation cost는 있음. 우리 데이터에도 간단한 action label을 붙여볼 수 있을지 검토.

author: 최민재
title: LLGformer: Learnable Long-range Graph Transformer for Traffic Flow Prediction
venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Web Conference
authors: Di Jin, Cuiying Huo, Jiayi Shi, Dongxiao He, Jianguo Wei and Philip S. Yu
abstract: Traffic prediction plays a pivotal role in intelligent transportation systems. Most existing studies only predict traffic flow for a specific time period based on traffic data from a short period, such as an hour, overlooking the influence of periodicity present in traffic data. Moreover, most of the existing advanced methods rely on manually constructed spatio-temporal graphs for joint modeling, or use pure spatial and pure temporal modules to separately model spatial and temporal features, which limits the learning of complex spatio-temporal patterns in traffic data due to structural inadequacies in the model. To address these issues, we propose a novel approach by constructing a learnable long-range spatio-temporal graph, which can better capture complex patterns in traffic data. We introduce a new model, LLGformer, which improves upon traditional Transformer-style models, facilitating more efficient learning of traffic flow data by integrating long-range historical information. Leveraging attention mechanisms on a spatiotemporal graph enables direct interaction of information across different time slices and locations. Additionally, we propose two optimization strategies to further boost the speed of training and inference. Extensive experiments on four real-world datasets show that the new model significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods.
content: Traffic prediction에서 기존 연구는 짧은 시간(예: 1시간)의 data로 특정 기간만 예측해서 traffic data의 periodicity 영향을 간과하고, 수작업으로 만든 spatio-temporal graph로 joint modeling하거나 pure spatial, pure temporal module을 따로 써서 복잡한 pattern 학습에 한계가 있음. 이를 해결하기 위해 learnable long-range spatio-temporal graph를 구성하고, Transformer-style model을 개선한 LLGformer를 제안함. Long-range historical information을 통합해 traffic flow를 효율적으로 학습하며, spatiotemporal graph 위의 attention으로 서로 다른 time slice와 location 사이의 정보가 직접 interact하게 함. 또 training과 inference 속도를 높이는 두 가지 optimization strategy도 제안함. 네 개의 real-world dataset 실험에서 SOTA를 크게 앞섰다고 보고함.
memo: Graph를 manual로 만들지 않고 learnable하게 한 건 Social-STGCNN의 fixed kernel adjacency와 대비되는 방향이라 흥미로움. Time slice와 location을 한 graph에서 attention으로 연결하는 구조는 pedestrian의 spatio-temporal interaction에도 가져올 수 있을 듯. Complexity가 커 보여서 optimization strategy 부분은 다시 읽어볼 것.

author: 최민재
title: Stochastic Trajectory Prediction via Motion Indeterminacy Diffusion
authors: Tianpei Gu; Guangyi Chen; Junlong Li; Chunze Lin; Yongming Rao; Jie Zhou; et al.
abstract: Human behavior has the nature of indeterminacy, which requires the pedestrian trajectory prediction system to model the multi-modality of future motion states. Unlike existing stochastic trajectory prediction methods which usually use a latent variable to represent multi-modality, we explicitly simulate the process of human motion variation from indeterminate to determinate. In this paper, we present a new framework to formulate the trajectory prediction task as a reverse process of motion indeterminacy diffusion (MID), in which we progressively discard indeterminacy from all the walkable areas until reaching the desired trajectory. This process is learned with a parameterized Markov chain conditioned by the observed trajectories. We can adjust the length of the chain to control the degree of indeterminacy and balance the diversity and determinacy of the predictions. Specifically, we encode the history behavior information and the social interactions as a state embedding and devise a Transformer-based diffusion model to capture the temporal dependencies of trajectories. Extensive experiments on the human trajectory prediction benchmarks including the Stanford Drone and ETH/UCY datasets demonstrate the superiority of our method. Code is available at https://github.com/gutianpei/MID.
content: Human behavior의 indeterminacy를 모델링하기 위해, 기존 latent variable 방식 대신 motion variation 과정을 indeterminate에서 determinate로 가는 reverse diffusion으로 formulation한 MID(Motion Indeterminacy Diffusion)를 제안함. Walkable area 전체의 indeterminacy를 점진적으로 제거해 원하는 trajectory에 도달하는 방식이며, observed trajectory로 conditioned된 parameterized Markov chain으로 학습됨. Chain 길이를 조절해 diversity와 determinacy의 균형을 조절할 수 있음. History와 social interaction을 state embedding으로 encoding하고 Transformer 기반 diffusion model로 temporal dependency를 잡음. Stanford Drone, ETH/UCY에서 우수한 성능을 보였다고 함.
memo: Pedestrian trajectory에 diffusion을 본격 적용한 논문 중 하나. Social GAN이나 Trajectron++ 같은 CVAE/GAN 계열보다 mode coverage가 좋다고 주장하는데 sampling step이 많아 real-time 적용은 부담일 것. Crosswalk에서 yield/go 두 mode를 diffusion으로 얼마나 잘 분리하는지 궁금함.

author: 최민재
title: Analysis and Prediction of Pedestrian Crosswalk Behavior during Automated Vehicle Interactions
authors: Suresh Kumaar Jayaraman; Dawn M. Tilbury; X. Jessie Yang; Anuj K. Pradhan; Lionel P. Robert
abstract: For safe navigation around pedestrians, automated vehicles (AVs) need to plan their motion by accurately predicting pedestrians trajectories over long time horizons. Current approaches to AV motion planning around crosswalks predict only for short time horizons (1-2 s) and are based on data from pedestrian interactions with human-driven vehicles (HDVs). In this paper, we develop a hybrid systems model that uses pedestrians gap acceptance behavior and constant velocity dynamics for long-term pedestrian trajectory prediction when interacting with AVs. Results demonstrate the applicability of the model for long-term (> 5 s) pedestrian trajectory prediction at crosswalks. Further we compared measures of pedestrian crossing behaviors in the immersive virtual environment (when interacting with AVs) to that in the real world (results of published studies of pedestrians interacting with HDVs), and found similarities between the two. These similarities demonstrate the applicability of the hybrid model of AV interactions developed from an immersive virtual environment (IVE) for real-world scenarios for both AVs and HDVs.
content: Automated vehicle(AV)이 보행자 주변에서 안전하게 주행하려면 긴 horizon에서 보행자 trajectory를 정확히 예측해야 하는데, 기존 crosswalk 주변 motion planning은 1-2초 정도의 짧은 horizon만 예측하고 human-driven vehicle(HDV)과의 interaction 데이터에 기반한다는 한계가 있음. 이 논문에서는 보행자의 gap acceptance behavior와 constant velocity dynamics를 결합한 hybrid systems model로 AV와 interaction하는 보행자의 long-term trajectory를 예측함. 결과적으로 crosswalk에서 5초 이상의 long-term 예측에 모델이 적용 가능함을 보임. 또 immersive virtual environment(IVE)에서 AV와 interact할 때의 crossing behavior를 기존 HDV 실제 연구 결과와 비교해 유사성을 확인했고, 이를 근거로 IVE 기반 모델이 real-world에도 적용 가능하다고 주장함.
memo: Deep learning 모델이 아니라 gap acceptance 기반 hybrid model이라 해석 가능성은 좋음. 하지만 constant velocity dynamics로 5초 이상 예측하는 건 deep model 대비 어느 정도인지 비교가 없어서 아쉬움. VR 데이터로 모델 만든 뒤 real world에 이식 가능하다는 주장은 내 연구에서도 참고할 만함.

author: 최민재
title: SocialVAE: Human Trajectory Prediction using Timewise Latents
authors: Pei Xu; Jean-Bernard Hayet; Ioannis Karamouzas
abstract: Predicting pedestrian movement is critical for human behavior analysis and also for safe and efficient human-agent interactions. However, despite significant advancements, it is still challenging for existing approaches to capture the uncertainty and multimodality of human navigation decision making. In this paper, we propose SocialVAE, a novel approach for human trajectory prediction. The core of SocialVAE is a timewise variational autoencoder architecture that exploits stochastic recurrent neural networks to perform prediction, combined with a social attention mechanism and a backward posterior approximation to allow for better extraction of pedestrian navigation strategies. We show that SocialVAE improves current state-of-the-art performance on several pedestrian trajectory prediction benchmarks, including the ETH/UCY benchmark, Stanford Drone Dataset, and SportVU NBA movement dataset. Code is available at: https://github.com/xupei0610/SocialVAE.
content: Pedestrian navigation decision의 uncertainty와 multimodality를 포착하기 위한 SocialVAE를 제안함. 핵심은 stochastic recurrent neural network를 활용하는 timewise variational autoencoder 구조로, 각 time step마다 latent를 두어 prediction을 수행함. 여기에 social attention mechanism과 backward posterior approximation을 결합해 보행자의 navigation strategy를 더 잘 추출하도록 함. ETH/UCY, Stanford Drone Dataset, SportVU NBA movement dataset에서 기존 SOTA를 개선했다고 보고함. NBA 데이터까지 포함해 pedestrian 외 domain으로의 확장 가능성도 보여줌.
memo: Trajectron++처럼 sequence 단위 latent가 아니라 timewise latent라서 중간에 마음을 바꾸는 행동(예: 갑자기 멈춤)을 표현하기 좋을 것 같음. Backward posterior 부분은 아직 완전히 이해 못 함, 수식 다시 볼 것. 횡단 중 stop-and-go 분석에 적용 가능성 있음.

author: 최민재
title: Transformer Networks for Trajectory Forecasting
authors: Francesco Giuliari; Irtiza Hasan; Marco Cristani; Fabio Galasso
abstract: Most recent successes on forecasting the people motion are based on LSTM models and all most recent progress has been achieved by modelling the social interaction among people and the people interaction with the scene. We question the use of the LSTM models and propose the novel use of Transformer Networks for trajectory forecasting. This is a fundamental switch from the sequential step-by-step processing of LSTMs to the only-attention-based memory mechanisms of Transformers. In particular, we consider both the original Transformer Network (TF) and the larger Bidirectional Transformer (BERT), state-of-the-art on all natural language processing tasks. Our proposed Transformers predict the trajectories of the individual people in the scene. These are "simple" model because each person is modelled separately without any complex human-human nor scene interaction terms. In particular, the TF model without bells and whistles yields the best score on the largest and most challenging trajectory forecasting benchmark of TrajNet. Additionally, its extension which predicts multiple plausible future trajectories performs on par with more engineered techniques on the 5 datasets of ETH + UCY. Finally, we show that Transformers may deal with missing observations, as it may be the case with real sensor data. Code is available at https://github.com/FGiuliari/Trajectory-Transformer.
content: 최근 people motion forecasting은 대부분 LSTM 기반이고 social interaction과 scene interaction을 모델링하는 방향으로 발전했는데, 이 논문은 LSTM의 사용 자체를 의문시하고 Transformer Network를 trajectory forecasting에 도입함. Step-by-step 순차 처리 대신 attention 기반 memory mechanism을 쓰며, original Transformer(TF)와 larger Bidirectional Transformer(BERT)를 모두 검토함. 각 사람을 독립적으로 모델링하는 simple model로, human-human이나 scene interaction term이 없음. 그럼에도 TF 모델은 TrajNet benchmark에서 best score를 기록하고, multiple future를 예측하는 확장 버전은 ETH+UCY 5개 dataset에서 engineered 기법들과 비슷한 성능을 보임. 또 missing observation도 다룰 수 있다고 함.
memo: Interaction term 없이도 TrajNet에서 best였다는 건, benchmark 자체가 social interaction을 충분히 요구하지 않는다는 얘기로도 읽힘. 그래서 벤치마크에서 interaction 모델이 얼마나 의미 있는지 다시 생각하게 됨. Missing observation에 robust하다는 점은 detection 기반 실제 데이터에서 유용할 듯함.

author: 최민재
title: Crowd-Robot Interaction: Crowd-aware Robot Navigation with Attention-based Deep Reinforcement Learning
authors: Changan Chen; Yuejiang Liu; Sven Kreiss; Alexandre Alahi
abstract: Mobility in an effective and socially-compliant manner is an essential yet challenging task for robots operating in crowded spaces. Recent works have shown the power of deep reinforcement learning techniques to learn socially cooperative policies. However, their cooperation ability deteriorates as the crowd grows since they typically relax the problem as a one-way Human-Robot interaction problem. In this work, we want to go beyond first-order Human-Robot interaction and more explicitly model Crowd-Robot Interaction (CRI). We propose to (i) rethink pairwise interactions with a self-attention mechanism, and (ii) jointly model Human-Robot as well as Human-Human interactions in the deep reinforcement learning framework. Our model captures the Human-Human interactions occurring in dense crowds that indirectly affects the robot's anticipation capability. Our proposed attentive pooling mechanism learns the collective importance of neighboring humans with respect to their future states. Various experiments demonstrate that our model can anticipate human dynamics and navigate in crowds with time efficiency, outperforming state-of-the-art methods.
content: 군중 속에서 robot이 효율적이면서 socially-compliant하게 이동하는 문제를 다룸. 기존 deep RL 방법은 문제를 one-way human-robot interaction으로 단순화해서 crowd가 커질수록 cooperation 능력이 떨어짐. 이를 넘어 Crowd-Robot Interaction(CRI)을 명시적으로 모델링하기 위해 (1) pairwise interaction을 self-attention으로 재구성하고, (2) human-robot interaction과 human-human interaction을 deep RL framework 안에서 함께 모델링함. 밀집 군중에서 일어나는 human-human interaction이 robot의 anticipation에 간접적으로 영향을 준다는 점을 반영한 것이며, attentive pooling이 이웃 인간들의 future state 관점에서 collective importance를 학습함. 실험에서 인간 dynamics를 anticipate하며 time-efficient하게 navigation해 SOTA를 앞섰다고 함.
memo: Trajectory prediction 쪽 social pooling의 아이디어가 RL로 넘어간 형태라 두 분야 연결 고리로 좋음. Human behavior를 simulator의 가정(ORCA 등)에 의존한다는 점이 가장 큰 한계일 듯. 만약 simulator의 pedestrian을 학습된 generative model로 교체하면 어떻게 되는지 해보고 싶음.

author: 최민재
title: Review of Pedestrian Trajectory Prediction Methods: Comparing Deep Learning and Knowledge-based Approaches
authors: Raphael Korbmacher; Antoine Tordeux
abstract: In crowd scenarios, predicting trajectories of pedestrians is a complex and challenging task depending on many external factors. The topology of the scene and the interactions between the pedestrians are just some of them. Due to advancements in data-science and data collection technologies deep learning methods have recently become a research hotspot in numerous domains. Therefore, it is not surprising that more and more researchers apply these methods to predict trajectories of pedestrians. This paper compares these relatively new deep learning algorithms with classical knowledge-based models that are widely used to simulate pedestrian dynamics. It provides a comprehensive literature review of both approaches, explores technical and application oriented differences, and addresses open questions as well as future development directions. Our investigations point out that the pertinence of knowledge-based models to predict local trajectories is nowadays questionable because of the high accuracy of the deep learning algorithms. Nevertheless, the ability of deep-learning algorithms for large-scale simulation and the description of collective dynamics remains to be demonstrated. Furthermore, the comparison shows that the combination of both approaches (the hybrid approach) seems to be promising to overcome disadvantages like the missing explainability of the deep learning approach.
content: Crowd scenario에서 보행자 trajectory 예측은 scene topology, pedestrian 간 interaction 등 여러 외부 요인에 좌우되는 어려운 문제임. 이 논문은 최근 급증한 deep learning 기반 예측 방법과 pedestrian dynamics 시뮬레이션에 널리 쓰이는 classical knowledge-based model(Social Force 계열 등)을 비교하는 literature review임. 두 접근법의 기술적, 응용적 차이를 정리하고 open question과 향후 방향을 다룸. 결론적으로 local trajectory 예측에서는 deep learning의 정확도가 높아 knowledge-based model의 pertinence가 의문스러워졌지만, large-scale simulation과 collective dynamics 기술 능력은 아직 입증되지 않았다고 봄. 두 방식을 합친 hybrid approach가 deep learning의 explainability 부족을 보완할 수 있어 유망하다고 정리함.
memo: Crowd dynamics 쪽(knowledge-based)과 CV/ML 쪽 시각을 한 번에 비교해줘서 입문용으로 좋았음. Hybrid approach가 유망하다는 결론은 내 방향(physics prior + generative model)과 일치해서 인용할 만함. Review라 실험적 근거는 약한 편이고, 구체적으로 어떤 hybrid 구조가 좋은지는 안 나옴.

author: 최민재
title: Learning Pedestrian Group Representations for Multi-modal Trajectory Prediction
authors: Inhwan Bae; Jin-Hwi Park; Hae-Gon Jeon
abstract: Modeling the dynamics of people walking is a problem of long-standing interest in computer vision. Many previous works involving pedestrian trajectory prediction define a particular set of individual actions to implicitly model group actions. In this paper, we present a novel architecture named GP-Graph which has collective group representations for effective pedestrian trajectory prediction in crowded environments, and is compatible with all types of existing approaches. A key idea of GP-Graph is to model both individual-wise and group-wise relations as graph representations. To do this, GP-Graph first learns to assign each pedestrian into the most likely behavior group. Using this assignment information, GP-Graph then forms both intra- and inter-group interactions as graphs, accounting for human-human relations within a group and group-group relations, respectively. To be specific, for the intra-group interaction, we mask pedestrian graph edges out of an associated group. We also propose group pooling&unpooling operations to represent a group with multiple pedestrians as one graph node. Lastly, GP-Graph infers a probability map for socially-acceptable future trajectories from the integrated features of both group interactions. Moreover, we introduce a group-level latent vector sampling to ensure collective inferences over a set of possible future trajectories. Extensive experiments are conducted to validate the effectiveness of our architecture, which demonstrates consistent performance improvements with publicly available benchmarks. Code is publicly available at https://github.com/inhwanbae/GPGraph.
content: 기존 pedestrian trajectory prediction은 개별 action set을 정의해 group action을 implicit하게 모델링하는 경우가 많은데, GP-Graph는 collective group representation을 명시적으로 쓰는 architecture로 기존 방법들에 plug-in 가능하다고 함. 핵심은 individual-wise와 group-wise relation을 모두 graph로 표현하는 것. 먼저 각 보행자를 가장 likely한 behavior group에 assign하고, 이 정보로 group 내 interaction(intra-group)과 group 간 interaction(inter-group) graph를 구성함. Intra-group은 group 밖 edge를 masking하고, group pooling & unpooling으로 여러 보행자를 하나의 node로 표현함. 마지막으로 두 group interaction feature를 합쳐 socially-acceptable한 future trajectory의 probability map을 추론하고, group-level latent vector sampling으로 한 group이 coherent한 future를 갖게 함. 공개 benchmark에서 consistent한 성능 향상을 보였다고 함.
memo: Social-STGCNN이나 SGCN은 pairwise edge 위주인데 group을 명시적으로 만든 점이 차별점. 횡단보도에서 함께 건너는 보행자 그룹은 한 덩어리로 움직이므로 이 구조가 잘 맞을 듯. Group assignment를 unsupervised로 학습하는데 해석 가능한 group이 실제로 나오는지는 qualitative를 더 봐야 함.

author: 최민재
title: Modeling Interactions of Autonomous Vehicles and Pedestrians with Deep Multi-Agent Reinforcement Learning for Collision Avoidance
authors: Raphael Trumpp; Harald Bayerlein; David Gesbert
abstract: Reliable pedestrian crash avoidance mitigation (PCAM) systems are crucial components of safe autonomous vehicles (AVs). The nature of the vehicle-pedestrian interaction where decisions of one agent directly affect the other agent's optimal behavior, and vice versa, is a challenging yet often neglected aspect of such systems. We address this issue by modeling a Markov decision process (MDP) for a simulated AV-pedestrian interaction at an unmarked crosswalk. The AV's PCAM decision policy is learned through deep reinforcement learning (DRL). Since modeling pedestrians realistically is challenging, we compare two levels of intelligent pedestrian behavior. While the baseline model follows a predefined strategy, our advanced pedestrian model is defined as a second DRL agent. This model captures continuous learning and the uncertainty inherent in human behavior, making the AV-pedestrian interaction a deep multi-agent reinforcement learning (DMARL) problem. We benchmark the developed PCAM systems according to the collision rate and the resulting traffic flow efficiency with a focus on the influence of observation uncertainty on the decision-making of the agents. The results show that the AV is able to completely mitigate collisions under the majority of the investigated conditions and that the DRL pedestrian model learns an intelligent crossing behavior.
content: Autonomous vehicle(AV)의 pedestrian crash avoidance mitigation(PCAM) 시스템에서 한 agent의 결정이 상대 agent의 optimal behavior에 직접 영향을 주는 vehicle-pedestrian interaction 측면은 중요하지만 간과되어 왔다는 문제의식에서 출발함. Unmarked crosswalk에서의 AV-pedestrian interaction을 MDP로 정의하고 AV의 PCAM 정책을 deep RL로 학습함. 보행자 모델링 수준을 두 단계로 비교하는데, baseline은 predefined strategy를 따르는 보행자이고, advanced 모델은 보행자를 또 하나의 DRL agent로 두어 continuous learning과 human behavior의 uncertainty를 반영함. 이로써 문제가 deep multi-agent RL(DMARL)이 됨. Collision rate와 traffic flow efficiency를 observation uncertainty의 영향 중심으로 평가했으며, 대부분 조건에서 AV가 collision을 완전히 mitigate하고 DRL 보행자는 intelligent한 crossing behavior를 학습한다고 보고함.
memo: 보행자를 RL agent로 두는 아이디어는 흥미롭지만, 학습된 pedestrian이 실제 사람의 crossing behavior와 얼마나 비슷한지 검증이 필요해 보임. 실제 trajectory data(예: Trajectron++로 예측한 분포)와 비교해서 realism를 평가하면 어떨까 싶음. Simulation 기반이라 점수는 보통.

author: 최민재
title: A Misclassification Framework for Identifying Systematic Error in Pedestrian Crash Prediction: Evidence from Seattle, WA
authors: Grace Douglas a , Stephen J. Mooney b , David M. Prendez b , Linda Ng Boyle a
abstract: Pedestrian crash prediction models often fail systematically, yet distinguishing correctable failures from random errors is challenging. We present a framework combining spatial clustering, temporal persistence, and model ensemble consensus to identify improvement opportunities. Applied to 13,706 Seattle intersections, the framework identified 141 high-priority locations (1.03%) exhibiting elevated temporal persistence, strong spatial clustering, and high ensemble consensus. A multiplicative priority score serves as a proxy for systematic error, concentrating 6.6% of total error into 1.03% of locations. The framework flagged crash-enriched intersections (roughly twice the baseline crash rate) where all models over-predicted risk, indicating the feature set captures that a location is hazardous but lacks the site-level descriptors needed to calibrate how much. Audits revealed three categories of omitted features: visual obstructions, static road use, and network complexity. Validation confirmed that adding these features reduced priority scores by 6.1% at high-priority locations, confirming that the framework correctly identifies where omitted context matters most.
content: Pedestrian crash prediction model이 systematic하게 실패하는 경우가 많은데, 고쳐질 수 있는 failure와 random error를 구분하기 어렵다는 문제를 다룸. Spatial clustering, temporal persistence, model ensemble consensus를 결합해 improvement opportunity를 찾는 framework를 제안함. Seattle의 13,706개 intersection에 적용해 141개(1.03%)의 high-priority location을 식별했고, 이 곳들은 temporal persistence가 높고 spatial clustering이 강하며 ensemble consensus가 높았음. Multiplicative priority score는 systematic error의 proxy로 쓰이며 전체 error의 6.6%를 1.03%의 location에 집중시킴. 이 intersection들은 crash가 baseline의 약 두 배로 많은데 모든 모델이 risk를 over-predict했고, feature set이 위험한 장소라는 것은 잡지만 얼마나 위험한지 calibration할 site-level descriptor가 부족하다는 의미로 해석함. Audit 결과 visual obstruction, static road use, network complexity의 세 가지 omitted feature 범주를 확인했고, 이를 추가하면 high-priority location의 priority score가 6.1% 감소해 framework의 유효성을 검증함.
memo: Error 분석 자체를 contribution으로 삼은 접근이 신선함. Over-predict되는 위치에서 omitted feature를 audit하는 과정은 trajectory prediction에서 failure case를 분석하는 방식과도 닮아서, 우리 모델의 failure를 scene별로 clustering해보는 데 참고할 만함. Seattle 한 도시 결과라 일반화는 확인 필요.

author: 최민재
title: Human Trajectory Prediction via Counterfactual Analysis
authors: Guangyi Chen; Junlong Li; Jiwen Lu; Jie Zhou
abstract: Forecasting human trajectories in complex dynamic environments plays a critical role in autonomous vehicles and intelligent robots. Most existing methods learn to predict future trajectories by behavior clues from history trajectories and interaction clues from environments. However, the inherent bias between training and deployment environments is ignored. Hence, we propose a counterfactual analysis method for human trajectory prediction to investigate the causality between the predicted trajectories and input clues and alleviate the negative effects brought by environment bias. We first build a causal graph for trajectory forecasting with history trajectory, future trajectory, and the environment interactions. Then, we cut off the inference from environment to trajectory by constructing the counterfactual intervention on the trajectory itself. Finally, we compare the factual and counterfactual trajectory clues to alleviate the effects of environment bias and highlight the trajectory clues. Our counterfactual analysis is a plug-and-play module that can be applied to any baseline prediction methods including RNN- and CNN-based ones. We show that our method achieves consistent improvement for different baselines and obtains the state-of-the-art results on public pedestrian trajectory forecasting benchmarks.
content: 기존 trajectory forecasting은 history trajectory의 behavior clue와 환경의 interaction clue로 future를 예측하지만, training과 deployment 환경 사이의 inherent bias를 무시함. 이 논문은 counterfactual analysis로 예측 trajectory와 input clue 사이의 causality를 분석하고 environment bias의 negative effect를 줄이려 함. 먼저 history trajectory, future trajectory, environment interaction으로 causal graph를 구성하고, trajectory 자체에 counterfactual intervention을 걸어 environment에서 trajectory로 가는 inference를 끊음. 이후 factual과 counterfactual trajectory clue를 비교해 environment bias 영향을 줄이고 trajectory clue를 강조함. RNN, CNN 기반 등 어떤 baseline에도 붙일 수 있는 plug-and-play module이며 공개 pedestrian trajectory benchmark에서 baseline마다 일관된 개선과 SOTA 결과를 보였다고 함.
memo: Plug-and-play라서 기존 모델(Social-STGCNN 같은) 위에 바로 얹어볼 수 있는 점이 실용적. 다만 causal graph가 단순해서 intervention의 의미가 얼마나 인과적인지는 의문. Environment shift(다른 도시 crosswalk)에 대한 robustness 검증용으로 시도해볼 만함.

author: 최민재
title: From Goals, Waypoints & Paths To Long Term Human Trajectory Forecasting
authors: Karttikeya Mangalam; Yang An; Harshayu Girase; Jitendra Malik
abstract: Human trajectory forecasting is an inherently multi-modal problem. Uncertainty in future trajectories stems from two sources: (a) sources that are known to the agent but unknown to the model, such as long term goals and (b)sources that are unknown to both the agent & the model, such as intent of other agents & irreducible randomness indecisions. We propose to factorize this uncertainty into its epistemic & aleatoric sources. We model the epistemic un-certainty through multimodality in long term goals and the aleatoric uncertainty through multimodality in waypoints& paths. To exemplify this dichotomy, we also propose a novel long term trajectory forecasting setting, with prediction horizons upto a minute, an order of magnitude longer than prior works. Finally, we presentY-net, a scene com-pliant trajectory forecasting network that exploits the pro-posed epistemic & aleatoric structure for diverse trajectory predictions across long prediction horizons.Y-net significantly improves previous state-of-the-art performance on both (a) The well studied short prediction horizon settings on the Stanford Drone & ETH/UCY datasets and (b) The proposed long prediction horizon setting on the re-purposed Stanford Drone & Intersection Drone datasets.
content: Human trajectory forecasting의 uncertainty를 epistemic(agent는 아는데 model은 모르는 long term goal 등)과 aleatoric(다른 agent의 intent, 비결정성 등) 두 source로 factorize하는 관점을 제안함. Epistemic uncertainty는 long term goal의 multimodality로, aleatoric uncertainty는 waypoint와 path의 multimodality로 모델링함. 이 구분을 보이기 위해 prediction horizon이 최대 1분에 이르는 새로운 long term trajectory forecasting setting도 제안함. 이를 구현한 scene-compliant 네트워크인 Y-net은 Stanford Drone, ETH/UCY의 short horizon과 re-purposed Stanford Drone, Intersection Drone의 long horizon setting 모두에서 기존 SOTA를 크게 개선했다고 함.
memo: PECNet의 goal-conditioned 아이디어를 scene segmentation과 결합해 발전시킨 느낌이고, uncertainty를 epistemic/aleatoric으로 나눈 해석이 설득력 있음. 개인적으로 가장 좋았던 점은 long horizon setting 제안. Intersection scene에서 보행자 goal은 사실상 crosswalk 반대편 curb라서 우리 데이터에 그대로 적용해볼 가치가 큼.

author: 최민재
title: Cross-cultural analysis of pedestrian group behaviour influence on crossing decisions in interactions with autonomous vehicles
authors: Sergio Martín Serrano; Óscar Méndez Blanco; Stewart Worrall; Miguel Ángel Sotelo; David Fernández-Llorca
abstract: Understanding cultural backgrounds is crucial for the seamless integration of autonomous driving into daily life as it ensures that systems are attuned to diverse societal norms and behaviours, enhancing acceptance and safety in varied cultural contexts. In this work, we investigate the impact of co-located pedestrians on crossing behaviour, considering cultural and situational factors. To accomplish this, a full-scale virtual reality (VR) environment was created in the CARLA simulator, enabling the identical experiment to be replicated in both Spain and Australia. Participants (N=30) attempted to cross the road at an urban crosswalk alongside other pedestrians exhibiting conservative to more daring behaviours, while an autonomous vehicle (AV) approached with different driving styles. For the analysis of interactions, we utilized questionnaires and direct measures of the moment when participants entered the lane. Our findings indicate that pedestrians tend to cross the same traffic gap together, even though reckless behaviour by the group reduces confidence and makes the situation perceived as more complex. Australian participants were willing to take fewer risks than Spanish participants, adopting more cautious behaviour when it was uncertain whether the AV would yield.
content: 자율주행의 사회적 수용성을 위해 문화적 배경 이해가 중요하다는 관점에서, 주변 보행자(co-located pedestrian)가 crossing behavior에 미치는 영향을 문화적, 상황적 요인과 함께 분석한 연구임. CARLA simulator 기반의 full-scale VR 환경을 만들어 스페인과 호주에서 동일한 실험을 반복함. 참가자 30명이 urban crosswalk에서 보수적인 행동부터 대담한 행동까지 보이는 다른 보행자들과 함께 길을 건너려 하고, AV는 서로 다른 driving style로 접근함. 설문과 lane에 진입한 시점의 direct measure로 분석한 결과, 보행자들은 같은 traffic gap을 함께 건너는 경향이 있으며 group의 reckless behavior는 confidence를 낮추고 상황을 더 복잡하게 인식하게 한다고 함. 또 호주 참가자가 스페인 참가자보다 위험을 덜 감수하고 AV가 yield할지 불확실할 때 더 신중했다고 보고함.
memo: Group 안에서 같은 gap을 함께 건넌다는 결과는 trajectory prediction에서 group-aware 모델(GP-Graph 같은)이 crosswalk에서 의미 있다는 근거가 됨. N=30이라 통계적 power는 약하고 두 나라만 비교해서 일반화는 조심해야 함. 문화 차이를 모델 feature로 넣을 수 있을지는 열린 질문.

author: 최민재
title: Visual-information-driven model for crowd simulation using temporal convolutional network
authors: Xuanwen Liang; Eric Wai Ming Lee
abstract: Crowd simulations play a pivotal role in building design, influencing both user experience and public safety. While traditional knowledge-driven models have their merits, data-driven crowd simulation models promise to bring a new dimension of realism to these simulations. However, most of the existing data-driven models are designed for specific geometries, leading to poor adaptability and applicability. A promising strategy for enhancing the adaptability and realism of data-driven crowd simulation models is to incorporate visual information, including the scenario geometry and pedestrian locomotion. Consequently, this paper proposes a novel visual-information-driven (VID) crowd simulation model. The VID model predicts the pedestrian velocity at the next time step based on the prior social-visual information and motion data of an individual. A radar-geometry-locomotion method is established to extract the visual information of pedestrians. Moreover, a temporal convolutional network (TCN)-based deep learning model, named social-visual TCN, is developed for velocity prediction. The VID model is tested on three public pedestrian motion datasets with distinct geometries, i.e., corridor, corner, and T-junction. Both qualitative and quantitative metrics are employed to evaluate the VID model, and the results highlight the improved adaptability of the model across all three geometric scenarios. Overall, the proposed method demonstrates effectiveness in enhancing the adaptability of data-driven crowd models.
content: Crowd simulation은 건물 설계, 사용자 경험, 공공 안전에 중요한데, 기존 data-driven crowd simulation model은 특정 geometry에 맞춰 설계되어 adaptability와 applicability가 떨어짐. 이를 해결하기 위해 scenario geometry와 pedestrian locomotion 등 visual information을 반영한 VID(visual-information-driven) crowd simulation model을 제안함. VID는 한 개인의 이전 social-visual information과 motion data를 바탕으로 다음 time step의 velocity를 예측함. Radar-geometry-locomotion 방식으로 보행자의 visual information을 추출하고, temporal convolutional network(TCN) 기반의 social-visual TCN으로 velocity를 예측함. Corridor, corner, T-junction의 세 공개 pedestrian motion dataset에서 qualitative, quantitative 평가를 했고 geometry가 달라도 adaptability가 향상되었다고 함.
memo: Trajectory prediction이 아니라 simulation 목적이라서 한 step velocity 예측 후 rollout하는 구조인데, 이때 error accumulation이 어떤지가 궁금함. Radar 방식의 visual feature는 Social-STGCNN의 거리 기반 graph보다 occlusion과 geometry를 자연스럽게 반영할 수 있어 보임. Crowd dynamics 쪽 evaluation metric을 어떻게 잡았는지는 다음에 자세히 볼 것.

author: 최민재
title: Personalized forward collision warning model with learning from human preferences
authors: Ning Xie a b , Rongjie Yu a b , Weili Sun c , Shi Qiu c , Kailun Zhong c , Ming Xu c , Guobin Wu c , Yi Yang c
abstract: The Forward Collision Warning (FCW) system has been widely equipped on vehicles to reduce rear-end crashes, which are considered the most common type of crash. However, existing FCW systems have the problem of low response rates, which restrict their safety improvement effects. This study aims to address this issue by building personalized FCW models based on human risk preferences. First, a warning feedback index ranks the gaps between drivers' risk perceptions and FCW models. Then, reward models are developed to characterize the risk perception preferences of each individual driver. After that, the reward models serve as guidelines to fine-tune the benchmark FCW model using the Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) algorithm. In the empirical analyses, a total of 95,814 warning fragments collected from 74 drivers are used, and the proposed method generates pseudo warning results. By comparing the pseudo and historical warnings, it shows that the precision of pseudo warning results increases from 53.5% to 78.2%. Furthermore, the average differences between the moment of warning and the moment of braking behavior decrease from 2.4 s to 1.6 s. This demonstrates a higher synchronization level in the timing of risk perception between the personalized FCW models and individual drivers, which enhances the driver's trust in the warning system.
content: Forward Collision Warning(FCW) system은 rear-end crash 감소를 위해 널리 장착되지만 low response rate 문제 때문에 안전 개선 효과가 제한적임. 이를 해결하기 위해 human risk preference 기반의 personalized FCW model을 구축함. 먼저 warning feedback index로 운전자의 risk perception과 FCW model 사이의 gap을 ranking하고, 각 운전자의 risk perception preference를 나타내는 reward model을 개발함. 이후 reward model을 guideline으로 삼아 benchmark FCW model을 Proximal Policy Optimization(PPO) algorithm으로 fine-tune함. 74명의 운전자에게서 수집한 95,814개의 warning fragment로 실증 분석을 했고, pseudo warning의 precision이 53.5%에서 78.2%로 증가했다고 함. 또 경고 시점과 braking 시점의 평균 차이도 2.4초에서 1.6초로 감소해 risk perception timing의 synchronization이 높아지고 운전자의 trust도 향상된다고 설명함.
memo: RLHF 방식(reward model + PPO)을 운전자 개인화에 가져온 점이 재밌음. 보행자 쪽에도 개인별 risk preference(예: 무단횡단 성향)를 reward로 학습해 pedestrian model을 personalize하는 것이 가능할 듯함. 평가가 pseudo warning과 historical warning 비교라서 실제 주행 효과 검증은 아닌 점이 아쉬움.

author: 최민재
title: PIP-Net: Pedestrian Intention Prediction in the Wild
authors: Mohsen Azarmi; Mahdi Rezaei; He Wang
abstract: Accurate pedestrian intention prediction (PIP) by Autonomous Vehicles (AVs) is one of the current research challenges in this field. In this article, we introduce PIP-Net, a novel framework designed to predict pedestrian crossing intentions by AVs in real-world urban scenarios. We offer two variants of PIP-Net designed for different camera mounts and setups. Leveraging both kinematic data and spatial features from the driving scene, the proposed model employs a recurrent and temporal attention-based solution, outperforming state-of-the-art performance. To enhance the visual representation of road users and their proximity to the ego vehicle, we introduce a categorical depth feature map, combined with a local motion flow feature, providing rich insights into the scene dynamics. Additionally, we explore the impact of expanding the camera's field of view, from one to three cameras surrounding the ego vehicle, leading to an enhancement in the model's contextual perception. Depending on the traffic scenario and road environment, the model excels in predicting pedestrian crossing intentions up to 4 seconds in advance, which is a breakthrough in current research studies in pedestrian intention prediction. Finally, for the first time, we present the Urban-PIP dataset, a customised pedestrian intention prediction dataset, with multi-camera annotations in real-world automated driving scenarios.
content: AV가 실제 도시 환경에서 보행자의 crossing intention을 예측하는 framework인 PIP-Net을 제안함. 카메라 마운트와 setup에 따라 두 variant를 제공함. Kinematic data와 driving scene의 spatial feature를 함께 쓰는 recurrent, temporal attention 기반 모델이며, 기존 SOTA를 앞섰다고 보고함. Road user의 시각적 표현과 ego vehicle과의 근접성을 높이기 위해 categorical depth feature map과 local motion flow feature를 도입함. 또 카메라 시야를 1개에서 3개로 넓혔을 때 contextual perception이 개선되는지도 분석함. 교통 상황에 따라 최대 4초 전에 crossing intention을 예측한다고 하고, 다중 카메라 annotation을 가진 Urban-PIP dataset도 처음으로 공개함.
memo: Coupling Intent and Action 같은 PIE/JAAD 기반 모델 대비 multi-camera와 depth feature를 쓴 게 실전적임. 4초 전 예측이 얼마나 정확한지는 precision-recall로 더 봐야 하고, false alarm 비율이 AV 적용에서는 중요할 것. Urban-PIP dataset은 확인해서 우리 연구에 쓸 수 있는지 볼 계획.

author: 최민재
title: Social-Implicit: Rethinking Trajectory Prediction Evaluation and The Effectiveness of Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation
authors: Abduallah Mohamed; Deyao Zhu; Warren Vu; Mohamed Elhoseiny; Christian Claudel
abstract: Best-of-N (BoN) Average Displacement Error (ADE)/ Final Displacement Error (FDE) is the most used metric for evaluating trajectory prediction models. Yet, the BoN does not quantify the whole generated samples, resulting in an incomplete view of the model's prediction quality and performance. We propose a new metric, Average Mahalanobis Distance (AMD) to tackle this issue. AMD is a metric that quantifies how close the whole generated samples are to the ground truth. We also introduce the Average Maximum Eigenvalue (AMV) metric that quantifies the overall spread of the predictions. Our metrics are validated empirically by showing that the ADE/FDE is not sensitive to distribution shifts, giving a biased sense of accuracy, unlike the AMD/AMV metrics. We introduce the usage of Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation (IMLE) as a replacement for traditional generative models to train our model, Social-Implicit. IMLE training mechanism aligns with AMD/AMV objective of predicting trajectories that are close to the ground truth with a tight spread. Social-Implicit is a memory efficient deep model with only 5.8K parameters that runs in real time of about 580Hz and achieves competitive results. Interactive demo of the problem can be seen at https://www.abduallahmohamed.com/social-implicit-amdamv-adefde-demo . Code is available at https://github.com/abduallahmohamed/Social-Implicit .
content: Trajectory prediction 평가에 가장 많이 쓰이는 Best-of-N(BoN) ADE/FDE는 생성된 sample 전체를 정량화하지 못해 모델 품질을 불완전하게 보여준다는 문제를 제기함. 이를 해결하는 Average Mahalanobis Distance(AMD)와 prediction의 overall spread를 재는 Average Maximum Eigenvalue(AMV) 두 metric을 제안함. ADE/FDE가 distribution shift에 둔감해 accuracy에 대한 biased한 감각을 준다는 점을 실험으로 보임. 또 기존 generative model 대신 Implicit Maximum Likelihood Estimation(IMLE)로 학습하는 Social-Implicit을 제안하는데, IMLE의 학습 방식이 AMD/AMV의 목표(GT에 가까우면서 spread가 작은 예측)와 일치함. 모델은 parameter가 5.8K에 불과한 memory efficient 구조이고 약 580Hz로 real-time 동작하며 competitive한 결과를 보인다고 함.
memo: Social-STGCNN 저자의 후속 작업이라 가볍게 만드는 방향은 일관됨. Best-of-20 ADE/FDE만 보는 관행에 문제 제기한 것이 이 논문의 핵심 기여라고 생각하고, 내 실험에서도 AMD/AMV를 같이 보고해야겠음. 5.8K parameter로 competitive하다는 점은 인상적이지만 큰 모델 대비 gap은 표를 다시 확인할 것.
